source_evidence.observation: Model 1 defines an input format with precision t, exponent range [e_min,e_max], unit roundoff u=2^(-t), extrema f_min and f_max, and underflow allowance g_min; it defines a wider accumulation format with T>=t, nested exponent range, unit roundoff U=2^(-T), extrema F_min and F_max, and underflow allowance G_min. Equation (2.3) models input rounding by fl(x)=x(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=u, |eta|<=g_min, eta*delta=0, assuming no overflow.

Equation (2.4) models each accumulation-format operation FL(x op y) as (x op y)(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=U, |eta|<=G_min, eta*delta=0. The paper explains that relative rounding and underflow error are mutually exclusive for an operation. Equations (2.3)-(2.4) default to round-to-nearest; directed rounding is covered only after replacing u,g_min,U,G_min by 2u,2g_min,2U,2G_min, respectively.

The underlying single-word analysis scales rows and columns using nonsingular diagonal Lambda and M. Their entries are powers of two so scaling introduces no rounding. The paper also assumes no underflow or overflow before scaling or after inverse scaling, with A, B, and C stored in sufficiently high precision to be represented exactly.

The overflow-preventing scale threshold is theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)). For the maximal power-of-two scaling used in the derivation, a nonzero row x and column y have factors satisfying theta/(2||x||_infty)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infty and theta/(2||y||_infty)<mu<=theta/||y||_infty. Consequently, their scaled maxima lie in (theta/2,theta].

The paper introduces a displayed lesssim bound by describing it as the result of dropping second-order terms from a preceding explicit inequality. This supplies the local convention needed to interpret the lesssim symbol later used in Theorem 4.1.

Section 4 defines p as the number of low-precision words and retains the p(p+1)/2 matrix products with nonnegative indices satisfying i+j<p. The scaled variant normalizes successive residuals by powers u^i to reduce underflow.

The scaled matrices Lambda A and BM are decomposed recursively into input-format matrices A^(i) and B^(j). The componentwise induction gives a residual bounded by the maximum of a relative term of order u^p and an underflow term of order u^(p-1)g_min.

Equations (4.18)-(4.20) give A=sum_{i=0}^{p-1}u^i Lambda^(-1)A^(i)+Delta A and B=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}u^j B^(j)M^(-1)+Delta B, with ||Delta A||_infty<=zeta||A||_infty, ||Delta B||_infty<=zeta||B||_infty, and zeta=max(u^p,2n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min). Equations (4.21)-(4.25) give the exact algebraic decomposition of the computed result into AB plus decomposition, accumulation, and omitted-product errors. Equation (4.26) bounds the omitted products by lesssim (p-1)u^p||A||_infty||B||_infty.

Equation (4.27) gives the accumulation estimate lesssim ((n+p^2)U+4rn theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infty||B||_infty, where r<=np(p+1)/2. Equation (4.28) combines the sources as 2zeta+zeta^2+(p-1)u^p+(n+p^2)U+2p(p+1)n^2theta^(-2)G_min. Theorem 4.1 specifies the recursive p-word algorithm and concludes equation (4.32), whose coefficient is (p+1)u^p+4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min+(n+p^2)U+2p(p+1)n^2theta^(-2)G_min. Equation (4.33) removes the two range-dependent terms.

The paper identifies terms of orders u^p and U as the range-unrestricted rounding terms and terms of orders u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min and theta^(-2)G_min as the additional input- and accumulation-underflow terms. It states that multiword arithmetic reduces the input rounding and input underflow errors by the same order-u^(p-1) factor.

binders: A is an m-by-n real matrix and B is an n-by-q real matrix; n is the shared inner dimension. The theorem does not explicitly state the domains of m,n,q beyond their use as matrix dimensions. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1.)

p is the number of words, with word indices i,j in {0,...,p-1}; its interpretation as a positive integer is inherited from Section 4 rather than explicitly quantified in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 8, printed B792, Section 4 and eqs. (4.1)-(4.3); PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.31).)

Lambda and M are diagonal power-of-two scaling matrices. Their conforming sizes are implicitly m-by-m and q-by-q because Lambda A and BM occur and their inverses are used. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1 and eq. (4.31).)

The inherited format parameters are t,T,e_min,e_max,E_min,E_max,u,U,f_min,f_max,F_min,F_max,g_min,G_min, with T>=t and [E_min,E_max] containing [e_min,e_max]. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1 and eqs. (2.1)-(2.3).)

A^(i) and B^(j) are input-format word matrices; Delta A and Delta B are their decomposition residuals, Delta C denotes accumulation error in the derivation, E is the total forward error, and C-hat is the computed matrix. (PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.18)-(4.25); PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1.)
hypotheses: The computation uses a mixed-precision MMA unit satisfying Model 1: inputs are rounded to the input format and inner-product operations use the accumulation format. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1; PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1.)
All entries of Lambda A and BM have magnitude at most theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)). (PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1.)

The derivation additionally uses maximal power-of-two row and column scaling: for each nonzero row x and column y, theta/(2||x||_infty)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infty and theta/(2||y||_infty)<mu<=theta/||y||_infty. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.15)-(4.20).)

The words are generated recursively by A^(i)=fl((Lambda A-sum_{k=0}^{i-1}u^k A^(k))/u^i) and B^(j)=fl((BM-sum_{k=0}^{j-1}u^k B^(k))/u^j), where fl rounds to the input format. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.30).)

Overflow is excluded by the arithmetic model and the chosen theta. The surrounding analysis also assumes no underflow or overflow in storage before scaling or after inverse scaling, and assumes A, B, and C are exactly represented in sufficiently high external precision. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, eq. (2.3); PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, scaling assumptions and eq. (3.2).)

The displayed parameters and bound use round-to-nearest. Directed rounding is a separate inherited variant requiring the substitutions u->2u, g_min->2g_min, U->2U, and G_min->2G_min. (PDF p. 3, printed B787, paragraph following eq. (2.4).)
conclusions: The computed result satisfies ||C-hat-AB||_infty lesssim ((p+1)u^p+4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min+(n+p^2)U+2p(p+1)n^2theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infty||B||_infty. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1 and eq. (4.32).)

Without range limitations, the comparison bound is ||C-hat-AB||_infty lesssim ((p+1)u^p+(n+p^2)U)||A||_infty||B||_infty. Thus the narrow-range result adds exactly the displayed input-underflow and accumulation-underflow terms. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.32)-(4.33); PDF p. 12, printed B796, comparison following eq. (4.33).)

Relative to the single-word bound, the paper's qualitative conclusion is that multiword arithmetic reduces both input-format rounding error and input-format underflow error by a factor of order u^(p-1), so neither is preferentially amplified. (PDF p. 12, printed B796, comparison of eq. (4.32) with eq. (3.26).)
definitions_and_conventions: theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)); f_max limits scaled inputs and sqrt(F_max/n) limits accumulation because an n-term inner product can reach n theta^2. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.2) and preceding paragraph.)

For the input format, u=2^(-t), f_min=2^(e_min), and f_max=2^(e_max)(2-2u). The underflow allowance is g_min=f_min/2 without subnormals and g_min=u f_min with gradual underflow. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1 and eq. (2.1).)

For the accumulation format, U=2^(-T), F_min=2^(E_min), and F_max=2^(E_max)(2-2U). The underflow allowance is G_min=F_min/2 without subnormals and G_min=U F_min with gradual underflow. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1 and eq. (2.2).)

Input rounding obeys fl(x)=x(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=u, |eta|<=g_min, eta*delta=0. Accumulation operations obey the analogous equation with U and G_min. (PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, eqs. (2.3)-(2.4).)
The decomposition-error coefficient is zeta=max(u^p,2n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min). (PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.20).)

The symbol lesssim denotes a simplified bound that omits second-order contributions; the selected pages do not give a formal universal-constant definition. (PDF p. 7, printed B791, paragraph introducing eq. (3.26); PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.27)-(4.33).)
implicit_context: The theorem is a summary of the Section 4 derivation and an extension of Theorem 3.1, so its short statement inherits the earlier exact-storage and scaling setup even though these assumptions are not all restated. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, scaling setup; PDF p. 11, printed B795, Section 4.2 introduction.)

The lower scaling bounds needed to derive lambda^(-1)<=2theta^(-1)||x||_infty and mu^(-1)<=2theta^(-1)||y||_infty come from the maximal scaling construction, not merely from the theorem's explicit upper bound on scaled entries. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.15)-(4.20).)

The sums with i+j

=p is restricted to the full grid 0<=i,j<=p-1. (PDF p. 8, printed B792, Section 4; PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.21)-(4.26).)

Equation (4.31) writes C=AB as the prescribed computation, while the following sentence denotes its finite-precision outcome by C-hat; AB remains the exact target in the error bound. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.31)-(4.32).)
statement.algorithm_linkage: First scale A by Lambda on the left and B by M on the right; recursively form p normalized residual words in the input format; compute the p(p+1)/2 products A^(i)B^(j) with i+j<p, using accumulation-format inner products; weight each product by u^(i+j); sum them; and apply Lambda^(-1) and M^(-1). The resulting finite-precision matrix is C-hat, and equation (4.32) applies specifically to this scaled, triangularly truncated p-word algorithm. (PDF p. 8, printed B792, Section 4 and eq. (4.3); PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.32).)
numerical_model: Input conversion and word extraction use the input-format operator fl with relative error bounded by u or mutually exclusive underflow error bounded by g_min. (PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, eq. (2.3) and its explanation; PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.30).)

Every inner product in every retained A^(i)B^(j) is computed in the accumulation format, whose operations have relative error bounded by U or mutually exclusive underflow error bounded by G_min. (PDF p. 3, printed B787, eq. (2.4); PDF p. 11, printed B795, text following eq. (4.31).)

The default mode is round-to-nearest. The directed-rounding extension changes all four error parameters by a factor of two rather than leaving equation (4.32) numerically unchanged. (PDF p. 3, printed B787, rounding-mode paragraph.)
The model permits either gradual underflow or absence of subnormals through the separate definitions of g_min and G_min, while excluding overflow. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, eqs. (2.1)-(2.3).)
error_notions: The selected conclusion is a normwise absolute forward-error bound for C-hat relative to exact AB; its coefficient can be read as normwise relative to ||A||_infty||B||_infty when that denominator is nonzero, but the theorem itself does not divide by it. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32).)
Delta A and Delta B represent input-format p-word decomposition errors and satisfy separate norm bounds with coefficient zeta. (PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.18)-(4.20).)

The exact algebraic total error contains -A Delta B-Delta A B+Delta A Delta B, the inverse-scaled accumulation error Lambda^(-1)Delta C M^(-1), and the negative sum of omitted products with i+j>=p. (PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.21)-(4.25).)

The four displayed first-order source classes in equation (4.32) are input/decomposition rounding, input underflow, accumulation rounding, and accumulation underflow. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32); PDF p. 12, printed B796, comparison following eq. (4.33).)

Because underflow terms depend on row and column infinity norms rather than componentwise products, the surrounding discussion treats the available result as normwise rather than componentwise. (PDF p. 8, printed B792, discussion preceding Section 4.)
norms: The conclusion uses ||C-hat-AB||_infty and scales it by ||A||_infty||B||_infty. These symbols must be preserved exactly. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32).)

Vector infinity norms occur in the maximal-scaling intervals and in the componentwise decomposition estimates. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.15)-(4.17).)
Absolute-value inequalities such as |A^(i)|<=(1+u)|Lambda A| are componentwise. (PDF p. 10, printed B794, sentence preceding eq. (4.26).)

The selected and surrounding passages do not explicitly define whether the matrix ||.||_infty notation is the induced row-sum norm or another infinity/max norm. (PDF p. 6, printed B790, text introducing eq. (3.24); PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32).)
constants_and_indexing: Word indices satisfy 0<=i,j<=p-1; residual indices satisfy 0<=k<i or 0<=k<j; retained products satisfy i+j<p. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.31).)
There are p(p+1)/2 retained word products. (PDF p. 8, printed B792, Section 4 definition.)
The omitted-product contribution is lesssim (p-1)u^p||A||_infty||B||_infty. (PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.26).)

If r is the maximum number of possible underflows while computing one output coefficient, then r<=np(p+1)/2. Substitution into 4rn theta^(-2)G_min gives the final coefficient 2p(p+1)n^2theta^(-2)G_min. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.27)-(4.28).)

The accumulation-rounding coefficient is n+p^2, not n+p(p+1)/2, and the input-underflow coefficient is exactly 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min in the displayed simplified theorem. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32).)
Only the inner dimension n occurs in the displayed coefficient; the outer dimensions m and q do not. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1 and eq. (4.32).)
higher_order_terms: Before the final simplification, equation (4.28) contains 2zeta+zeta^2+(p-1)u^p in addition to the accumulation terms. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.28).)

Substituting zeta=max(u^p,2n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min), bounding the maximum by the sum, and dropping zeta^2 yields the first two displayed terms (p+1)u^p and 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min. (PDF p. 10, printed B794, eq. (4.20); PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.28) and (4.32).)

The lesssim estimates in equations (4.26), (4.27), (4.28), and (4.32) are not exact inequalities with all higher-order terms and constants displayed. (PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795, eqs. (4.26)-(4.32); PDF p. 7, printed B791, explanation preceding eq. (3.26).)
Equation (4.33) is a range-unrestricted comparison, not an additional term in equation (4.32). (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.32)-(4.33).)
exceptional_values: Overflow is outside the rounding model and is assumed not to occur; theta is selected to prevent overflow in both input storage and intermediate accumulation. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, eq. (2.3); PDF p. 5, printed B789, derivation of eq. (3.2).)
Underflow is explicitly included, both with gradual subnormals and without subnormals, through g_min and G_min. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, eqs. (2.1)-(2.2).)
A single operation incurs either a relative rounding error or an underflow error, not both, because eta*delta=0. (PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, eqs. (2.3)-(2.4) and following explanation.)

The theorem is formulated for real matrices and does not provide semantics or bounds for NaNs or infinities. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1's real-arithmetic rounding model.)

undebatable_constraints: The exact matrix dimensions A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x q), with n as the inner dimension, must be retained. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1.)

The target must be the computed result of the scaled, recursively normalized, triangularly truncated p-word algorithm in equations (4.29)-(4.31), not arbitrary matrix multiplication or an unscaled multiword product. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.31).)

The scale threshold must be theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)), and the derivation relies on maximal power-of-two scaling intervals, not merely an arbitrary upper bound. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.2) and (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 10, printed B794, eqs. (4.15)-(4.20).)
Input word extraction must use the input format, while every retained matrix-product inner product must use the accumulation format. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eqs. (4.29)-(4.31).)
The final coefficient must preserve all four terms and their constants: (p+1)u^p, 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min, (n+p^2)U, and 2p(p+1)n^2theta^(-2)G_min. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32).)
The right side must be multiplied by ||A||_infty||B||_infty and the conclusion must remain a normwise forward-error statement. (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32).)

The conclusion uses lesssim and drops higher-order terms; it must not be strengthened silently to an exact <= inequality with constant one. (PDF p. 7, printed B791, explanation of simplified bounds; PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32).)
Overflow exclusion, the two possible underflow regimes, and the mutually exclusive relative/underflow error model must be retained. (PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, eqs. (2.1)-(2.4).)
Round-to-nearest is the default scope; directed rounding requires doubling the four model parameters as stated by the paper. (PDF p. 3, printed B787, rounding-mode paragraph.)

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 4.1 states only that scaled entries are bounded above by theta, whereas the derivation requires maximal scaling and corresponding lower bounds.
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem's hypothesis says only that elements of Lambda A and BM are bounded by theta (PDF p. 11, printed B795, Theorem 4.1). Equations (3.4a)-(3.4b) impose theta/(2||x||_infty)<lambda and theta/(2||y||_infty)<mu, and equations (4.15)-(4.20) use the resulting inverse-factor bounds (PDF p. 5, printed B789; PDF p. 10, printed B794).
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract must either inherit the maximal-scaling condition from Section 3 or flag the theorem statement as under-specified; arbitrary much smaller power-of-two scales satisfy the stated upper bound but do not justify the displayed underflow estimate.

ambiguities.issue: The matrix infinity norm is used but not explicitly defined in the selected or surrounding passages.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper moves from coefficientwise estimates to a choice of matrix norm and then displays ||.||_infty without defining whether it is induced row-sum or entrywise maximum (PDF p. 6, printed B790, text and eq. (3.24)); Theorem 4.1 reuses the same notation (PDF p. 11, printed B795, eq. (4.32)).
ambiguities.impact: A formalization should preserve the paper's norm symbol or justify a particular matrix-norm definition independently; choosing an inequivalent norm silently can change dimension factors.

ambiguities.issue: The notation for the accumulation error Delta C is internally unclear between equations (4.21)-(4.24) and equation (4.27).
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (4.21) and (4.24) place Delta C inside Lambda^(-1)(... )M^(-1), so its contribution is Lambda^(-1)Delta C M^(-1) (PDF p. 10, printed B794). Equation (4.27) instead prints a bound for ||Delta C||_infty directly in terms of unscaled ||A||_infty||B||_infty (PDF p. 11, printed B795).
ambiguities.impact: The final theorem bound is unambiguous, but reconstructing the intermediate proof requires deciding whether equation (4.27) silently denotes the inverse-scaled accumulation error or omits those factors typographically.

ambiguities.issue: The lesssim relation has only an informal local explanation.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper says equation (3.26) is obtained by dropping second-order terms (PDF p. 7, printed B791), while equations (4.26)-(4.33) use lesssim without specifying an explicit hidden constant or listing every omitted term (PDF pp. 10-11, printed B794-B795).
ambiguities.impact: The source supports a first-order simplified estimate, not a literal exact inequality with a specified constant. A formal target must state how lesssim and omitted terms are represented.

ambiguities.issue: The arithmetic used to form residual sums, subtractions, and divisions inside equations (4.29)-(4.30) is not assigned a separate floating-point format.
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (4.29)-(4.30) place a single input-format fl around each complete residual expression but do not annotate the internal sum, subtraction, or division operations (PDF p. 11, printed B795).
ambiguities.impact: The most direct reading treats the interior expression mathematically and rounds only its result. An implementation that rounds every internal operation would require additional error terms not present in the stated contract.

ambiguities.issue: The theorem does not explicitly quantify p or address zero rows and columns in the maximal-scaling formulas.
ambiguities.evidence: Section 4 calls p the number of words and indexes 0 through p-1 (PDF p. 8, printed B792), but Theorem 4.1 does not state p>=1 (PDF p. 11, printed B795). Equations (3.4a)-(3.4b) divide by ||x||_infty and ||y||_infty and therefore do not apply literally to zero rows or columns (PDF p. 5, printed B789).
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement needs positive-integer dimension and word-count assumptions and a harmless separate convention for scaling zero rows or columns.

contract_plain_english: For real A of size m-by-n and B of size n-by-q, use the paper's maximal power-of-two row and column scaling so every scaled input is at most theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)). Decompose each scaled matrix into p input-format words by repeatedly normalizing and rounding the residual, retain exactly the products with nonnegative indices i+j<p, compute all their inner products in the accumulation format, and undo the scaling. Under Model 1, round-to-nearest, no overflow, and the inherited exact external-storage assumptions, the computed C-hat has normwise forward error lesssim ((p+1)u^p+4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min+(n+p^2)U+2p(p+1)n^2theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infty||B||_infty. The first and third terms are the range-unrestricted rounding contributions; the second and fourth are the additional input- and accumulation-underflow contributions. The lesssim sign is essential because the paper has dropped second-order terms, including the displayed zeta^2 contribution from the preceding estimate. (PDF pp. 10-12, printed B794-B796, eqs. (4.18)-(4.33) and their comparison.)
